description: Synchronize data between spreadsheets and databases: map columns to fields, define sync direction, configure triggers, handle type conversions, manage conflicts, and verify the result.

steps.description: Map spreadsheet columns to database fields, noting data type differences and naming mismatches.

inputs.name: spreadsheet-structure
inputs.desc: Column names, data types, and sample values from the spreadsheet

inputs.name: database-schema
inputs.desc: Table and field definitions from the target database

outputs.name: field-mapping
outputs.desc: Column-to-field mapping with data type conversions noted

outputs.name: mapping-exceptions
outputs.desc: Columns or fields that do not have a clear match

process: List every spreadsheet column with its inferred data type and a sample value.
List every database field with its defined type and constraints.
Match columns to fields by name similarity and data type compatibility.
Flag any column or field without a match as an exception to resolve.

steps.description: Define whether the sync runs one-way (spreadsheet to database or database to spreadsheet) or bidirectionally, and set the conflict resolution policy.

inputs.name: field-mapping
inputs.desc: Column-to-field mapping from the schema mapper

inputs.name: sync-requirements
inputs.desc: Business rules for which system is the source of truth and how conflicts should resolve

outputs.name: sync-direction
outputs.desc: One-way or bidirectional, with the designated source of truth

outputs.name: conflict-policy
outputs.desc: Rules for handling conflicts (last-write-wins, source-wins, manual review)

process: Determine which system is the primary source of truth for each field.
Choose one-way sync if one system always owns the data, bidirectional if both systems create or update records.
Define the conflict resolution policy for overlapping updates.
Document the sync direction and conflict rules.

steps.description: Configure when the sync runs: on a schedule, on change detection, or manually.

inputs.name: sync-direction
inputs.desc: The chosen sync direction and source of truth

outputs.name: trigger-configuration
outputs.desc: Trigger type, schedule or event definition, and retry policy

outputs.name: sync-frequency
outputs.desc: How often the sync runs under normal conditions

process: Assess how frequently the source data changes and how quickly the target needs to reflect it.
Choose the trigger type: scheduled (cron), event-driven (on row change or webhook), or manual.
Define the retry policy for failed syncs.
Document the trigger configuration and expected sync frequency.

steps.description: Handle data type conversions between the spreadsheet and database (dates, numbers, booleans, enums, text).

inputs.name: field-mapping
inputs.desc: Column-to-field mapping with type differences noted

outputs.name: conversion-rules
outputs.desc: Specific conversion logic for each field pair with type differences

outputs.name: validation-checks
outputs.desc: Checks to run after conversion to verify data integrity

process: For each field pair with a type mismatch, define the conversion function (e.g., text date to ISO 8601, string to integer, yes/no to boolean).
Handle edge cases: empty cells, malformed values, values outside the target type range.
Write validation checks that run after conversion to flag bad data.
Document the conversion rules.

steps.description: Define how the sync handles errors: logging, alerts, partial rollback, and retry.

outputs.name: error-handling-plan
outputs.desc: How each category of error is logged, alerted, retried, or escalated

outputs.name: rollback-policy
outputs.desc: Whether a failed sync rolls back the batch or skips the bad record

process: Categorize possible errors: connection failures, type conversion failures, constraint violations, conflicts.
For each category, define the response: retry, skip and log, alert, or abort and rollback.
Set up the error log with enough detail to diagnose issues after the fact.
Document the error handling plan and rollback policy.

steps.description: Verify the sync by comparing source and target after a run to confirm data integrity.

outputs.name: sync-setup-document
outputs.desc: Complete sync configuration including mapping, direction, triggers, conversions, error handling, and verification

outputs.name: verification-results
outputs.desc: Results of the initial sync verification (record counts, spot checks, discrepancy list)

process: Run the sync against a test dataset or a small batch of live data.
Compare record counts between source and target.
Spot-check a sample of records for field-level accuracy.
Document the results and flag any discrepancies for investigation.

description: Automate manual data entry from one system to another: identify sources and targets, define mappings and transformations, configure triggers, validate before entry, and log results.

steps.description: Identify the data sources (where data comes from) and targets (where data goes), including access methods and data formats.

inputs.name: current-manual-process
inputs.desc: Description of the current manual data entry process, including what is entered, from where, and into what

inputs.name: system-access-details
inputs.desc: API endpoints, file locations, or UI paths for source and target systems

outputs.name: source-inventory
outputs.desc: List of data sources with access method, format, and frequency of new data

outputs.name: target-inventory
outputs.desc: List of target systems with access method, required fields, and validation rules

process: List every source the manual process reads from (files, emails, web pages, other systems).
List every target the manual process writes to (databases, spreadsheets, SaaS platforms).
For each source and target, document the access method (API, file drop, screen entry) and data format.
Note any authentication or rate limiting constraints.

steps.description: Define the field mapping and transformation rules from source to target.

inputs.name: source-inventory
inputs.desc: Data sources with format and field details

inputs.name: target-inventory
inputs.desc: Target systems with required fields and validation rules

outputs.name: field-mapping-rules
outputs.desc: Source-to-target field mapping with any transformation logic (format, concatenate, split, default)

outputs.name: unmapped-fields
outputs.desc: Source fields with no target and target fields with no source, requiring manual handling or defaults

process: Match source fields to target fields by name, meaning, and data type.
Define transformations where the formats differ (date formats, name splitting, unit conversion).
Identify target required fields that have no source and define default values or manual fill rules.
Document the complete mapping.

steps.description: Configure what triggers the automated entry: new source record, updated record, or scheduled batch.

inputs.name: source-inventory
inputs.desc: Source system details including data change frequency

outputs.name: entry-trigger
outputs.desc: Trigger type (event-driven or scheduled), polling interval or event definition, and batch size

outputs.name: deduplication-rules
outputs.desc: How to detect and skip records that have already been entered

process: Determine whether the source supports event notifications (webhooks, change feeds) or requires polling.
Choose event-driven triggers for real-time needs, scheduled batch for periodic bulk entry.
Define the deduplication logic to prevent double entry (unique key check, timestamp comparison).
Document the trigger configuration.

steps.description: Validate each record before writing it to the target system.

outputs.name: validation-rules
outputs.desc: Pre-entry checks for each field (type, range, format, required, referential integrity)

outputs.name: rejection-handling
outputs.desc: What happens to records that fail validation (quarantine queue, alert, skip and log)

process: For each target field, define the validation rule (type check, range check, format pattern, not-null).
Add cross-field validations where business rules require it (e.g., end date after start date).
Define the handling for records that fail: quarantine for manual review, skip and log, or reject and alert.
Document the validation rules and rejection handling.

steps.description: Log every entry attempt with its outcome (success, failure, skipped) for audit and troubleshooting.

inputs.name: validation-rules
inputs.desc: The validation checks applied to each record

outputs.name: entry-log-schema
outputs.desc: Fields captured in the entry log (timestamp, source record ID, target record ID, status, error detail)

outputs.name: data-entry-automation-document
outputs.desc: Complete documentation of the automated data entry setup

process: Define the log schema: timestamp, source record identifier, target record identifier, status (success, failed, skipped), error detail.
Configure the log storage (database table, log file, or monitoring system).
Set up alerts for error rate thresholds (e.g., more than 5% failure in a batch).
Compile the full automation documentation: sources, targets, mappings, triggers, validation, logging.

description: Clean and standardize messy data: profile the dataset, define cleaning rules, apply them, validate the result, and produce the cleanup report.

steps.description: Profile the dataset to identify quality issues: null rates, duplicates, format inconsistencies, outliers, and type mismatches.

inputs.name: dataset-location
inputs.desc: Path or connection string to the dataset to clean

inputs.name: expected-schema
inputs.desc: Expected column names, types, and value ranges

outputs.name: profiling-report
outputs.desc: Per-column statistics: null rate, duplicate rate, distinct count, min/max, format distribution, outlier count

outputs.name: issue-inventory
outputs.desc: Categorized list of data quality issues found

process: Compute basic statistics for each column: row count, null count, distinct values, min, max, mean (numeric), mode.
Check for duplicate rows and near-duplicate rows (fuzzy match on key fields).
Identify format inconsistencies within each column (mixed date formats, inconsistent casing, trailing whitespace).
Flag outliers using statistical methods (z-score, IQR) for numeric columns.
Compile the profiling report and issue inventory.

steps.description: Define the cleaning rules for each category of issue found in profiling.

inputs.name: issue-inventory
inputs.desc: Categorized list of data quality issues

outputs.name: cleaning-rules
outputs.desc: Ordered list of cleaning operations with their logic (standardize, deduplicate, fill, flag, correct)

outputs.name: priority-ranking
outputs.desc: Issues ranked by impact on downstream use

process: For format inconsistencies, define the standard format and the transformation to apply.
For duplicates, define the matching criteria and the merge or keep strategy (keep newest, merge fields).
For nulls, decide per column: fill with a default, fill from another source, flag for review, or drop the row.
For outliers, decide: cap at a threshold, flag for review, or leave as-is if legitimate.
Rank the rules by their impact on data usability.

steps.description: Apply the cleaning rules to the dataset in the defined order.

inputs.name: dataset-location
inputs.desc: Path or connection to the dataset

outputs.name: cleaned-dataset-location
outputs.desc: Path or connection to the cleaned dataset

outputs.name: cleaning-log
outputs.desc: Record of every change made: row, column, old value, new value, rule applied

process: Back up the original dataset before making changes.
Apply the cleaning rules in priority order, logging each change.
Track the number of rows and fields affected by each rule.
Save the cleaned dataset to the target location.

steps.description: Validate the cleaned dataset against business rules and compare quality metrics to the original.

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Pass/fail on each business rule, plus before/after quality metrics comparison

outputs.name: data-cleanup-report
outputs.desc: Summary of what was cleaned, how many records changed, quality improvement metrics, and remaining issues

process: Re-run the profiling on the cleaned dataset and compare metrics to the original (null rate, duplicate rate, format consistency).
Run the business validation rules (required fields populated, referential integrity, value ranges).
Compile the cleanup report: issues found, rules applied, records changed, quality improvement, remaining issues.
Flag any remaining issues that require manual attention.

description: Reconcile data between two systems: extract datasets, match records, identify and classify discrepancies, investigate, and produce the reconciliation report.

steps.description: Extract the datasets from both systems for comparison, normalizing formats and timestamps.

inputs.name: system-a-connection
inputs.desc: Connection details and query for the first system

inputs.name: system-b-connection
inputs.desc: Connection details and query for the second system

outputs.name: dataset-a
outputs.desc: Extracted and normalized dataset from system A

outputs.name: dataset-b
outputs.desc: Extracted and normalized dataset from system B

process: Connect to system A and extract the dataset for the reconciliation period.
Connect to system B and extract the corresponding dataset.
Normalize both datasets to a common format (date formats, currency, identifiers).
Verify row counts and date ranges match the expected scope.

steps.description: Match records between the two datasets using the defined keys and flag discrepancies.

outputs.name: matched-records
outputs.desc: Records that matched on the key fields, with any field-level differences noted

outputs.name: discrepancy-list
outputs.desc: Unmatched and mismatched records, classified by type (missing in A, missing in B, value mismatch)

process: Define the matching keys (transaction ID, date plus amount, or composite key).
Run the match: inner join on keys to find matched records, outer join to find unmatched.
For matched records, compare every non-key field and flag differences.
Classify discrepancies: missing in A, missing in B, or present in both with value mismatch.

steps.description: Investigate each discrepancy to determine the cause and resolution.

inputs.name: discrepancy-list
inputs.desc: Classified list of unmatched and mismatched records

outputs.name: investigation-results
outputs.desc: Cause and resolution for each discrepancy (timing, data entry error, system bug, legitimate difference)

outputs.name: correction-actions
outputs.desc: List of corrections to apply in each system to resolve the discrepancies

process: For missing records, check whether the record was created after the extraction cutoff (timing issue) or is genuinely absent.
For value mismatches, trace the data back to the original entry or transaction to identify the correct value.
Classify each discrepancy cause: timing, data entry error, system bug, rounding, or legitimate difference.
Define the correction action for each resolvable discrepancy.

steps.description: Produce the reconciliation report with summary statistics, discrepancy detail, and recommended actions.

inputs.name: correction-actions
inputs.desc: Corrections to apply in each system

outputs.name: reconciliation-report
outputs.desc: Summary of matched records, discrepancies found, causes, corrections applied, and remaining open items

outputs.name: process-improvements
outputs.desc: Recommendations to prevent recurring discrepancies

process: Summarize the reconciliation: total records, matched count, discrepancy count by category.
List each discrepancy with its cause and resolution status.
Identify patterns in the discrepancies that suggest a systemic issue.
Recommend process or system changes to reduce future discrepancies.

description: Build reusable report templates: define the structure, connect data sources, configure calculations, design the layout, and set up the refresh mechanism.

steps.description: Define the report structure: sections, metrics, and visualizations for each section.

inputs.name: report-purpose
inputs.desc: What question the report answers and who reads it

inputs.name: available-data-sources
inputs.desc: Data sources the report can pull from (databases, APIs, spreadsheets)

outputs.name: report-outline
outputs.desc: Ordered list of sections with the metrics and visual types for each

outputs.name: data-requirements
outputs.desc: Fields and aggregations needed from each data source

process: Identify the audience and the decisions the report informs.
List the metrics and KPIs the report must show.
Group the metrics into logical sections (summary, detail, trend, comparison).
For each section, choose the visual type (table, bar chart, line chart, single number, heatmap).

steps.description: Connect the report template to its data sources and define the queries.

outputs.name: data-connections
outputs.desc: Configured connections and queries for each data source

outputs.name: calculation-definitions
outputs.desc: Formulas and aggregations applied to raw data to produce the report metrics

process: For each data source, set up the connection (credentials, endpoint, query).
Write the query or extraction logic for each metric.
Define the calculated fields and aggregations (ratios, running totals, year-over-year).
Test each connection and query with sample data.

steps.description: Design the visual layout: page structure, branding, headers, and conditional formatting.

outputs.name: layout-template
outputs.desc: Visual layout with positioning, sizing, color coding, and conditional formatting rules

outputs.name: formatting-rules
outputs.desc: Conditional formatting and alerting rules (red if below target, green if above)

process: Arrange sections on the page in order of importance (key takeaways first).
Apply consistent formatting: fonts, colors, number formats, date formats.
Add conditional formatting for thresholds (red/yellow/green for KPIs).
Include headers, footers, timestamps, and data freshness indicators.

steps.description: Set up how and when the report refreshes its data.

outputs.name: refresh-schedule
outputs.desc: When the report refreshes (daily, hourly, on-demand) and the distribution list

outputs.name: report-template-documentation
outputs.desc: Complete documentation: structure, data sources, calculations, layout, refresh schedule, and usage guide

process: Set the refresh cadence based on how often the underlying data changes and how quickly the audience needs updates.
Configure the distribution method (email, shared dashboard, file drop).
Set up error notifications if a refresh fails.
Compile the template documentation for future maintainers.

description: Import data from external files into a system: validate the file, map columns, preview, run the import with error handling, and verify the result.

steps.description: Validate the incoming file's format, structure, encoding, and basic data quality.

inputs.name: import-file
inputs.desc: The file to import (CSV, Excel, JSON, XML)

inputs.name: target-system-schema
inputs.desc: The target system's expected fields, types, and constraints

outputs.name: file-profile
outputs.desc: File format, encoding, row count, column count, and detected data types

outputs.name: structural-issues
outputs.desc: Any issues with the file structure (missing headers, inconsistent row lengths, encoding errors)

process: Detect the file format (CSV, Excel, JSON, XML) and character encoding.
Parse the headers and count the rows and columns.
Check for structural issues: missing headers, ragged rows, embedded delimiters, truncated data.
Profile each column for data type and null rate.

steps.description: Map the file's columns to the target system's fields, with type conversion rules.

inputs.name: file-profile
inputs.desc: File structure and detected data types

outputs.name: import-mapping
outputs.desc: File column to target field mapping with conversion rules

outputs.name: unmapped-columns
outputs.desc: File columns that do not map to any target field

process: Auto-match columns to target fields by name similarity.
For unmatched columns, present them for manual mapping or exclusion.
Define type conversion rules for each mapped pair.
Flag required target fields that have no source column.

steps.description: Preview a sample of the import to catch errors before running the full batch.

outputs.name: preview-results
outputs.desc: First N records as they would appear in the target, with any conversion warnings

outputs.name: preview-errors
outputs.desc: Records that failed validation during preview

process: Apply the mapping and conversion rules to the first 10-50 records.
Display the transformed records as they would appear in the target system.
Flag any records that fail validation (type errors, constraint violations, required fields null).
Ask for confirmation before proceeding to the full import.

steps.description: Run the full import with error handling and progress tracking.

inputs.name: preview-results
inputs.desc: Confirmed preview with no blocking errors

outputs.name: import-summary
outputs.desc: Total records processed, succeeded, failed, and skipped

outputs.name: error-log
outputs.desc: Detail for each failed record (row number, field, error)

process: Run the import in batches, committing each batch on success.
For each failed record, log the error and continue to the next record.
Track progress: records processed, succeeded, failed, remaining.
On completion, report the summary and error log.

steps.description: Verify the imported data by comparing counts, spot-checking records, and running integrity checks.

inputs.name: import-summary
inputs.desc: Counts of processed, succeeded, and failed records

outputs.name: verification-report
outputs.desc: Comparison of source file row count to target record count, spot-check results, and integrity check results

outputs.name: import-record
outputs.desc: Complete import record: file, mapping, preview, execution summary, verification, and error log

process: Compare the source file row count to the target system record count for this import.
Spot-check a random sample of records for field-level accuracy.
Run referential integrity checks if the imported data references other tables.
Compile the complete import record.

description: Conduct a pivot table analysis: define the question, select the data, configure dimensions, calculate aggregations, identify patterns, and produce the report.

steps.description: Define the analysis question and identify the data source.

inputs.name: analysis-question
inputs.desc: The business question the pivot analysis should answer

inputs.name: available-datasets
inputs.desc: Datasets available for analysis with their schemas

outputs.name: question-definition
outputs.desc: Precisely stated question with the expected answer format (number, ranking, trend, comparison)

outputs.name: selected-dataset
outputs.desc: The dataset to use, with relevant columns identified

process: Restate the business question in precise, measurable terms.
Identify which dataset contains the data needed to answer the question.
Select the relevant columns from that dataset.
Note any filtering needed (date range, segment, status).

steps.description: Configure the pivot dimensions: rows, columns, values, and filters.

outputs.name: pivot-configuration
outputs.desc: Row fields, column fields, value fields with aggregation functions, and filter conditions

outputs.name: aggregation-methods
outputs.desc: Aggregation function for each value field (sum, count, average, min, max, median)

process: Choose the row dimension (the primary grouping, e.g., product, region, month).
Choose the column dimension if a cross-tabulation is needed (e.g., month across columns).
Select the value fields and their aggregation functions (sum revenue, count orders, average rating).
Apply filters to scope the analysis (date range, category, status).

steps.description: Execute the pivot calculation and produce the result table.

inputs.name: pivot-configuration
inputs.desc: Rows, columns, values, filters, and aggregations

outputs.name: pivot-table
outputs.desc: The computed pivot table with row totals, column totals, and grand total

outputs.name: derived-metrics
outputs.desc: Calculated metrics added to the pivot (percentage of total, rank, cumulative sum)

process: Apply filters to the dataset.
Group by the row and column dimensions, computing the aggregation for each cell.
Add row totals, column totals, and grand total.
Calculate derived metrics: percentage of total, rank, cumulative sum as needed.

steps.description: Identify patterns, trends, and outliers in the pivot results.

outputs.name: pattern-findings
outputs.desc: Notable patterns, trends, and outliers with their significance

outputs.name: pivot-analysis-report
outputs.desc: Complete analysis report: question, methodology, pivot table, findings, and recommendations

process: Scan for the highest and lowest values in each dimension.
Look for trends across the column dimension (growth, decline, seasonality).
Identify outliers that deviate from the group pattern.
Write the findings as clear statements with supporting numbers.
Compile the analysis report with the question, method, table, and findings.

description: Archive old data from active systems: define criteria, identify records, export to archive storage, verify integrity, remove from active, and produce the archival record.

steps.description: Define which records qualify for archival based on age, status, and access frequency.

inputs.name: system-description
inputs.desc: The active system and its data model

inputs.name: retention-requirements
inputs.desc: Legal, regulatory, and business retention rules for each data type

outputs.name: archival-criteria
outputs.desc: Rules that determine when a record is eligible for archival (age, status, last access date)

outputs.name: exclusion-rules
outputs.desc: Records that must never be archived regardless of age (active cases, open transactions)

process: Review the retention requirements for each data type in the system.
Define the age threshold for archival (e.g., closed records older than 2 years).
Add status-based criteria (only closed, completed, or inactive records).
Define exclusion rules for records that must remain active regardless of age.

steps.description: Query the active system to identify records that match the archival criteria.

outputs.name: archival-candidate-list
outputs.desc: List of records eligible for archival with key fields and counts

outputs.name: archival-size-estimate
outputs.desc: Estimated storage size of the archival batch

process: Run the archival criteria query against the active system.
Apply the exclusion rules to remove ineligible records.
Summarize the candidate list: record count by type, date range, and estimated storage size.
Review the candidate list for anything unexpected before proceeding.

steps.description: Export the archival candidates to the archive storage, preserving data integrity.

inputs.name: archival-size-estimate
inputs.desc: Expected size of the archive batch

outputs.name: archive-location
outputs.desc: Where the archived data is stored (path, bucket, database)

outputs.name: export-manifest
outputs.desc: List of exported records with checksums for integrity verification

process: Export the records to the archive storage in a format that preserves all fields and relationships.
Generate checksums for each exported batch or file.
Record the export manifest: record IDs, export timestamp, destination, checksums.
Verify the export completed without errors.

steps.description: Verify the archive by comparing record counts, checksums, and spot-checking data.

inputs.name: archive-location
inputs.desc: Where the archived data is stored

inputs.name: export-manifest
inputs.desc: List of exported records with checksums

outputs.name: integrity-results
outputs.desc: Verification results: record count match, checksum match, spot-check pass/fail

outputs.name: removal-authorization
outputs.desc: Confirmation that the archive is verified and records can be removed from the active system

process: Compare the archive record count to the export manifest count.
Verify checksums match between the export and the archive.
Spot-check a random sample of archived records against the active system originals.
If all checks pass, authorize removal from the active system.

steps.description: Remove the verified archived records from the active system and produce the archival record.

inputs.name: removal-authorization
inputs.desc: Confirmation that the archive is verified

outputs.name: removal-log
outputs.desc: List of records removed from the active system with timestamps

outputs.name: archival-record
outputs.desc: Complete archival documentation: criteria, candidates, export, verification, removal, and archive location

process: Remove the archived records from the active system in batches.
Log each removal: record ID, removal timestamp, archive location.
Verify the active system record count decreased by the expected amount.
Compile the complete archival record for audit purposes.
